Index.meta_title: Inferon — real cost numbers for every LLM request
Index.meta_description: An OpenAI-compatible gateway that meters, guards and routes your model traffic with true cost visibility and automatic budget protection.

Hero.title: Know the <important>true cost</important> of every LLM request.
Hero.description: Inferon meters, guards and routes your model traffic with real cost numbers and automatic budget protection — through a drop-in OpenAI-compatible API.

Features.section_title: Everything you need to trust your LLM spend
Features.section_description: A metering gateway that stays out of the way — your existing OpenAI client keeps working.
Features.feature1_description: Every request records its tokens and upstream USD cost, rendered as exact decimal strings — never a float.
Features.feature2_description: Per-tenant budgets with an automatic circuit breaker that degrades safely instead of blowing the limit.
Features.feature3_description: Validates and repairs tool-call output, transparently falling back to a frontier model when needed.
Features.feature4_description: Point your client at /v1/chat/completions and keep your existing SDK, keys and request shapes.
Features.feature5_description: Mint and revoke API keys per tenant from the dashboard; only hashes are ever stored.
Features.feature6_description: Humans sign in with GitHub into signed-cookie sessions; teammates join by invite with their own keys.

CTA.title: Ready to see your real spend?
CTA.description: Sign in with GitHub and get a tenant with its first API key in seconds.

SignIn.meta_description: Sign in to Inferon with GitHub.

DashboardLayout.meta_description: Your Inferon cost and routing dashboard.

DashboardIndexPage.title_bar_description: One view of the last {days} days: spend, recoverable waste, response quality, the proxy’s own overhead and the dataset your traffic produced.
DashboardIndexPage.limit_error: Could not update the limit — please retry.
DashboardIndexPage.empty_body: Point your SDK at Inferon to see spend, breakdowns and limits here.
DashboardIndexPage.no_waste: No cost leaks detected in {requests} requests.
DashboardIndexPage.no_data: No data for this window yet.
DashboardIndexPage.performance_empty: No measured requests yet — the first one fills this in.
DashboardIndexPage.report_unavailable: This report could not be loaded just now. Its own page is still available.
DashboardIndexPage.datasets_empty: No verified examples yet — the dataset page shows why traffic did not qualify.
DashboardIndexPage.attention_errors: Error rate is above the line — check the fallback chain and guard
DashboardIndexPage.attention_latency: p95 time to first token is far above the line — pick a faster model
DashboardIndexPage.attention_waste: Spend the audit can recover — cap or re-route it
DashboardIndexPage.attention_lint: Payload waste the lint has priced — enable pruning
DashboardIndexPage.requests_help: Every request the proxy served in this window.
DashboardIndexPage.total_cost_help: What those requests cost at the upstream providers' prices, after routing, fallback and caching.
DashboardIndexPage.total_savings_help: What the router, the fallback chain and the provider cache avoided, priced against running the frontier model every time.
DashboardIndexPage.p95_ttft_help: Time to the first token, 95th percentile: 95% of responses started faster than this.
DashboardIndexPage.error_rate_help: Failed requests in this window, as a share of all requests; the quality report breaks it down by class.

KeysPage.key_once: This is the only time the key is shown; only its hash is stored.
KeysPage.no_keys: No keys yet — create your first one above.

OperatorPage.title_bar_description: Platform-wide usage over the last {days} days.
OperatorPage.no_data: No data for this window yet.
OperatorPage.requests_help: Every request routed through the proxy in this window, across all tenants.
OperatorPage.errors_help: Requests that failed in this window, from any cause (upstream, timeout, guard or proxy).
OperatorPage.total_cost_help: Upstream spend across all tenants in this window.

ProvidersPage.title_bar_description: Bring your own upstream account — the proxy runs on your key.
ProvidersPage.empty: No provider yet — traffic uses the shared platform key.
ProvidersPage.name: Name
ProvidersPage.key_note: Encrypted at rest and never shown again — only a masked hint is kept.
ProvidersPage.owner_only: Only the tenant owner can manage providers.
ProvidersPage.error: Could not update providers — please retry.
ProvidersPage.rotate_key_note: Leave blank to keep the current key; enter a new one to rotate it.
ProvidersPage.headers_note: One `Name: Value` per line, sent on every upstream request.
ProvidersPage.models_error: Could not read the model list from the provider.
ProvidersPage.local_note: A model on your own network. Inference costs $0 here, but the cloud must be able to reach this URL (TLS if it is public). Only the endpoint you expose is touched — the rest of your LAN stays private.
ProvidersPage.key_optional: Leave blank if the endpoint needs no key
ProvidersPage.local_free: Free — served on your own hardware

QualityPage.title_bar_description: How often responses were usable — derived from the response, plus your thumbs when supplied.
QualityPage.success_rate_help: Responses that were non-empty and did not fail, refuse or truncate.
QualityPage.empty_rate_help: A 200 response with no content — usually a token budget spent on reasoning.
QualityPage.truncated_rate_help: The completion hit its max_tokens before it finished.
QualityPage.guard_fallback_rate_help: Structured output that failed its schema contract and was replayed on the frontier model.

RoutingPage.title_bar_description: Set an ordered fallback chain used when a request fails.
RoutingPage.help: When the primary model fails retryably (a transport error, 429, or 5xx), Inferon retries with the next model. A request problem (4xx) is never retried.
RoutingPage.primary_help: the model your request asks for
RoutingPage.empty: No fallback — a failing request surfaces the error.
RoutingPage.owner_only: Only the tenant owner can change routing.
RoutingPage.error: Could not save routing — please retry.
RoutingPage.tier_pairs_help: Send simple traffic on a frontier model to the cheap model you name — your own local model included. Your pairs win over the built-in ones.
RoutingPage.tier_pairs_empty: No pairs — the built-in table applies (gpt-4o → gpt-4o-mini, deepseek-v4-pro → deepseek-flash).
RoutingPage.tier_pairs_inactive: inactive — a model is not enabled
RoutingPage.tier_pairs_error: Could not save tier pairs — please retry.
RoutingPage.triggers_help: By default a step handles transport errors, 429s and 5xx. Mark Guard on a step only if the schema guard should replay a failed structured response to it instead of the built-in frontier replay.
RoutingPage.audit_help: Who changed a routing, budget or payload control, and when. Newest first; entries are append-only.
RoutingPage.audit_empty: No changes since the audit trail started.

ControlsPage.cheap_help: Used when 85% of the budget is spent.
ControlsPage.guard: Schema guard (validate and repair tool-call output)
ControlsPage.threshold_help: Complexity below this is downgraded to the cheap tier (0–1).
ControlsPage.owner_only: Only the tenant owner can change these controls.
ControlsPage.capture: Store raw prompts and completions (dataset pairs)
ControlsPage.capture_help: Off = costs, outcomes and aggregates are still recorded, but no payload is stored and nothing qualifies for a dataset.
ControlsPage.retention_help: Older payloads are purged by a periodic pass; 0 keeps them indefinitely.
ControlsPage.lint_help: Advisory checks before dispatch: they never change the request, they only record what looks wasteful and price it. Choose which ones you want.

SettingsPage.title_bar_description: Your workspace in one place: connect a client, manage keys and members, and see who you are signed in as.
SettingsPage.connect_body: Mint a key, point your SDK at the proxy, and send the first request.
SettingsPage.related_body: Everything else that changes how requests are served.
SettingsPage.keys_help: Create, inspect and revoke the keys your clients use. The raw key is shown once.
SettingsPage.members_help: Invite teammates by GitHub login. They join as members on their next sign-in.
SettingsPage.connect_key_step_help: Your key authenticates the API. It is shown once — copy it now.
SettingsPage.connect_create_key_failed: Could not create the key — please retry.
SettingsPage.connect_key_once: This is the only time your key is shown. Copy it now:
SettingsPage.connect_model_help: The model id your first request calls. Pick one you enabled, or type your provider’s own id.
SettingsPage.connect_links_help: Models live with the provider that serves them.

SpendReportPage.title_bar_description: Every dollar over the last {days} days — by model, provider, API key and system prompt.
SpendReportPage.transactions_help: A transaction is every request that shared one X-Inferon-Session-Id — an agentic loop, a chat thread, a batch run.

AuditPage.title_bar_description: Six findings computed from your last {days} days of traffic. Refreshes every 15 seconds.
AuditPage.no_traffic_title: No traffic in this window yet
AuditPage.no_traffic_body: Point your SDK at the Inferon proxy and this report fills itself in from your own requests.
AuditPage.f1_desc: Frontier models handling tiny requests (<100 input / <50 output tokens) that a cheaper tier handles identically.
AuditPage.f2_desc: Frontier models on plain unstructured text — no tools, schema or structured output.
AuditPage.f3_desc: The same large prompt repeated without the provider cache paying off.
AuditPage.f4_desc: What the router and fallback chain already recovered versus running the frontier model.
AuditPage.f5_desc: Which model, provider and key actually drove the spend.
AuditPage.f6_desc: Requests you pay for that are empty, refused, truncated or failing — and why.
AuditPage.share_body: Create a read-only link. It shows the six findings — never prompts, keys or completions — and you can revoke it at any time.
AuditPage.share_once: Copy this link now — it is shown once.
AuditPage.public_body: A read-only report generated from live traffic. Refreshes every 15 seconds.
AuditPage.invalid_body: It may have been revoked, or the address is wrong.

DatasetsPage.title_bar_description: Verified examples from production traffic: how many, what they cost, why the rest did not qualify, and a JSONL download.
DatasetsPage.grouping_help: Task clusters group prompts by meaning; the exact hash groups byte-identical prompts.
DatasetsPage.spend_help: Across the window, including excluded traffic
DatasetsPage.empty: No captured pairs yet. Traffic with a stored completion and no thumbs-down qualifies; check that raw payload storage is on.
DatasetsPage.purge_confirm: Delete every stored payload now? Costs are kept; pairs are not.
DatasetsPage.clusters_help: Groups of prompts by hash or by meaning, depending on the grouping.
DatasetsPage.excluded_help: Traffic that did not qualify: a missing completion, a thumbs-down or a failed request.

PruningPanel.help: Opt-in. Exact duplicate turns are removed before dispatch, and (with a budget) the oldest turns beyond it. Tool definitions, the system prompt and the last turn are never touched. A schema-contract request is never rewritten. A holdout is sent unpruned so the effect is measurable, and a quality regression turns the policy off automatically.
PruningPanel.budget_placeholder: e.g. 8000 — leave blank for no budget
PruningPanel.budget_help: Estimated at characters ÷ 4. The oldest non-system, non-last turns go first.
PruningPanel.holdout_help: Share of requests sent unpruned, as the control arm. Clamped at 50%.
PruningPanel.owner_only: Only the tenant owner can change pruning.
PruningPanel.error: Could not save pruning — please retry.

EvalsPage.title_bar_description: Score a model against a pinned gold set from your own verified traffic, and gate a change before you trust it.
EvalsPage.gold_help: A gold set is an immutable copy of verified examples: the exact inputs and their reference answers. Later retention or pruning cannot change what a run measured.
EvalsPage.no_gold: No gold set yet — pin one from your qualified examples.
EvalsPage.run_help: The run is bounded by case count and spend, and never touches production aggregates, budgets or routing.
EvalsPage.gate_help: Compare a challenger against a baseline. Below 20 scored cases, or with an incomplete run, there is no verdict.
EvalsPage.need_two_runs: Run at least two models to compare them.
EvalsPage.owner_only: Only the tenant owner can run evals.

PromptsPage.title_bar_description: Name a prompt, see every version your traffic produced, and diff two of them. Read-only: a label never edits a prompt or deletes a trace.
PromptsPage.name: Name
PromptsPage.hash_placeholder: the system prompt hash, from a dataset cluster
PromptsPage.label: Name this version
PromptsPage.none: No named prompts yet — name a content hash to start tracking versions.
PromptsPage.content_unavailable: This tenant does not capture payloads, so there is no content to diff. The counts still work.
PromptsPage.owner_only: Only the tenant owner can name a prompt.

RuntimePage.title_bar_description: Is the proxy fast? Its own overhead against the sub-millisecond claim, the end-to-end latency around it, and where in time and model it degrades.
RuntimePage.claim_p95: p95 overhead < 5 ms (guard against a cache regression)
RuntimePage.claim_window: Evaluated on this build: the last {hours} h ({samples} sample(s), observed p50 {observed}). The cards above describe the window you selected.
RuntimePage.claim_note: Measured as proxy_us: request start to just before the first upstream dispatch, so the upstream and the response body are excluded. Warm requests are those within the hot-path cache TTLs; the first request after an idle period pays the config load.
RuntimePage.heatmap_help: 95th-percentile total latency and error rate per model per bucket. A dot is no traffic — not a fast day. Values are printed in every cell; the tint is a hint.
RuntimePage.no_samples: No measured requests in this window.
RuntimePage.overhead_help: proxy_us: request start to just before the first upstream dispatch. Excludes the upstream and the response body.
RuntimePage.under_1ms_help: Share of measured requests whose own overhead stayed under the 1 ms claim.
RuntimePage.samples_help: Requests with a measured overhead in this window — the denominator for every number on this page.
RuntimePage.total_help: End to end, from request start to the last byte of the response.
RuntimePage.ttft_help: Request start to the first token of the response.
RuntimePage.legend_healthy: No tint: under 5% errors and p95 under 3 s
RuntimePage.legend_degraded: Light tint: 5%+ errors or p95 over 3 s
RuntimePage.legend_failing: Dark tint: 20%+ errors or p95 over 10 s
RuntimePage.legend_empty: dot: no traffic in the bucket

PayloadsPage.title_bar_description: What happens to prompts and completions: whether they are stored and for how long, what the lints found, what pruning removed, and which PII shapes were detected. Counts only — never a value.
PayloadsPage.capture_off_help: Payloads are not stored: only cost, latency and outcomes.
PayloadsPage.capture_help: Whether raw prompts and completions are stored at all, and for how long. Costs, latency and outcomes are always kept.
PayloadsPage.lint_help: Two passes: one before dispatch (repeated prompts, oversized schemas, boilerplate, duplicate turns) and the cost rules after the trace lands. Advisory — the payload is forwarded unchanged.
PayloadsPage.pruning_help: Opt-in rewriting of redundant context, with a holdout arm so the effect on quality is measured. A schema-contract request is never rewritten.
PayloadsPage.pruning_off: Pruning is off: every payload is forwarded unchanged.
PayloadsPage.pii_help: Pattern detection on stored payloads. Counts only — a matched value is never recorded, and this is not a compliance guarantee.
PayloadsPage.lint_coverage_help: Requests the pre-flight lint actually inspected, out of all traffic in the window.
PayloadsPage.lint_findings_help: Pre-flight findings in this window, and the spend their waste was priced at.
PayloadsPage.prune_removed_help: Requests whose context was rewritten by the pruning policy.
